correctness.rationale: Positive synchronous histories reduce exactly to the scalar recurrence. The two-step maximum strictly decreases whenever the maximum is positive, including on the boundary of the nonnegative box, which excludes a positive limiting maximum by compactness. The consecutive positive ratios obey the stated two-step Möbius recurrence: for all sufficiently late n it maps positive ratios into [1/3,2], has a uniform derivative bound below one there, and tends to a map fixing 1, so both parity ratios tend to 1. Matching the cubic and quintic terms in R(f(t),t)=f(f(t))+O(t^7) gives f(t)=t-t^3/3+t^5/9. The derivative of R(s,t)-f(s) in s tends to -1/2, so the graph error divided by u_n^7 stays bounded: u_{n+1}/u_n tends to 1 and therefore does not undo the uniform contraction. The controlled inverse-square increment is 2/3+1/(9w_n)+O(w_n^-2); first averaging and then summing the reciprocal correction yields w_n=2n/3+O(log n) and the summable error after subtracting 2/3+(1/6)log(1+1/n). The increment formula for u, shifted one step, gives -sqrt(3/8) for the scaled lag. This is an all-positive-history result only on the synchronous branch. value.rationale: The symmetric critical branch is an invariant and natural boundary of the competition model, not a fitted parameter slice. The clock distinguishes logarithmic drift in the actual iteration count from qualitative attraction or a leading n^-1/2 decay, and the universal lag amplitude measures a separate observable of the delay dynamics. Control of the stable graph for all positive synchronous histories makes these coefficients usable beyond a local formal expansion. No claims are made for unequal-species histories.
